remediation: Disallow DTDs and external entity/schema access.

remediation: Accept only a bounded arithmetic grammar and never call eval.

description: A pickle payload invokes an attacker-selected callable.
remediation: Reject executable serialization and use a typed JSON contract.

description: A logged-in user retrieves another account by identifier.
remediation: Check ownership against the authenticated server-side principal.

description: Unrestricted profile updates overwrite a privileged role.
remediation: Allowlist user-editable profile properties.

description: An authenticated state change ignores the anti-CSRF token.
remediation: Require the synthetic server-side session token, validate the request and ASCII token types, and compare safely. Non-ASCII strings and invalid JSON types are rejected without an exception.

description: Login upgrades an attacker-selected session identifier into a real authenticated session.
remediation: Remove the pre-login session and issue a fresh identifier that resolves to the authenticated principal. Trusted observers inspect session state, verify real logout and require unrelated sessions and legitimate login to remain functional.

tests.name: second trusted principal can log in

description: Working password records use unsalted fast MD5 in the vulnerable variant.
remediation: Store an explicit salted scrypt record and verify passwords against persisted records. The trusted oracle independently recomputes the fixture profile (n=16384, r=8, p=1, 32-byte key); calibrate a production policy separately.

tests.name: stored password works and wrong password fails
separate password records use separate salts

description: An embedded maintenance password grants access.
remediation: Remove the embedded credential and require an independently configured secret. Fail closed when absent; validate input types and compare strict UTF-8 bytes so configured Unicode passwords work. Synthetic environment configuration is trusted test metadata.

description: Account-derived reset tokens permit a public guess to authenticate against the actual token store.
remediation: Issue CSPRNG tokens while preserving issuance, validation and one-time consumption. A trusted observer checks usability, replay rejection, unrelated state and repeated issuance. Finite tests do not certify entropy; this in-memory fixture does not model expiration or concurrent requests.

description: An untrusted username forges an extra audit event.

description: Authentication logs retain a supplied password.

description: A download handler checks the first URL decoding pass but reads a path after a second pass. Nested percent encodings can disclose a real synthetic file outside public/. Inspired by EDB-50406; this is an original laboratory model of the specified boundary, not a reproduction of the affected product.
remediation: Decode to a bounded stable form before validation, reject residual encodings and backslashes, then resolve and enforce containment in public/. Reads use real local files. The model covers disclosure only, not Apache CGI execution; concurrent filesystem mutation is outside this fixture.

description: An item name is concatenated into a text template before compilation. A bounded, original arithmetic template engine evaluates embedded expressions instead of displaying the name as data. Inspired by EDB-52030; this is an original laboratory model of the specified boundary, not a reproduction of the affected product.
remediation: Compile only the trusted template and substitute the name as a value. The teaching engine implements integer addition, subtraction and multiplication via AST, with size and node limits; it has no Python eval, attribute access, filesystem access or code execution. The EDB report demonstrates expression evaluation; this fixture makes no claim about further impact or the vendor engine.

description: A CGI query parameter is URL-decoded and inserted into a serialized HTTP Location header. CRLF sequences create extra headers or terminate the header block. Inspired by EDB-49923; this is an original laboratory model of the specified boundary, not a reproduction of the affected product.
remediation: Reject every control character after query decoding and before response serialization. This is a response-serialization fixture with no live HTTP server or browser; it demonstrates header/body boundaries, not script execution.

references.title: EDB-49923 — CHIYU TCP/IP Converter devices — CRLF injection (sirpedrotavares)

description: An outbound handler validates a DNS answer, then resolves again at connection time. A deterministic resolver changes from a public address to an internal address and a synthetic transport exposes an internal service marker. Inspired by EDB-52651; this is an original laboratory model of the specified boundary, not a reproduction of the affected product.
remediation: Validate all returned addresses and pass the chosen validated address directly to the transport, preserving the original host separately. The resolver sequences and transport are trusted fixture dependencies, not request parameters. This is a handler model: no DNS, socket, TLS or HTTP request occurs; production code also needs redirect, proxy and TLS policy.

references.title: EDB-52651 — flyto_core 2.26.7 — DNS rebinding SSRF (Jorge González Milla)

description: An authenticated SVG upload follows href and xlink:href resources during server-side processing. A real XML parser feeds an offline endpoint registry and can retrieve synthetic internal content. Inspired by EDB-52551; this is an original laboratory model of the specified boundary, not a reproduction of the affected product.
remediation: Preflight the entire SVG and permit only local fragment references; reject external resources before any fetch. The strict policy also rejects external public images. Authentication is a synthetic tenant-admin token. This bounded handler model parses SVG references but does not render images, execute scripts, perform network requests or reproduce ThingsBoard.

references.title: EDB-52551 — ThingsBoard 4.2.0 — SVG resource SSRF / CVE-2025-34282 (9tamilmathi)

description: An authenticated remote-file import accepts internal destinations and writes returned synthetic content into actual download files. URL parsing, address resolution and endpoint fetching are separate operations. Inspired by EDB-51030; this is an original laboratory model of the specified boundary, not a reproduction of the affected product.
remediation: Preflight every URL and all resolved addresses, reject non-global destinations, and pass the validated address to the offline fetch dependency. Invalid mixed batches produce no files. This handler model uses a fixed trusted DNS/endpoint registry, never external DNS or HTTP; it does not model redirects, proxies, TLS or CVAT task processing.

references.title: EDB-51030 — CVAT — remote-file SSRF / CVE-2022-31188 (Emir Polat)

description: An upload constructs and parses a real in-memory TAR archive. Lexically valid member names can follow an earlier archive symlink to overwrite a synthetic file outside unpacked/. Inspired by EDB-43002; this is an original laboratory model of the specified boundary, not a reproduction of the affected product.
remediation: Preflight every parsed TAR member, accept regular files only, reject symlinks in destination parents and enforce resolved containment before extraction. The local harness confines even the vulnerable link targets to its working directory. No Documentum code is included; concurrent filesystem mutation and hard-link extraction are outside this bounded fixture.

references.title: EDB-43002 — OpenText Documentum Content Server — TAR symlink traversal / CVE-2017-15276 (Andrey B. Panfilov)

description: A factoryBypass query parameter creates an administrator session without credentials. A successful request updates a real SQLite configuration row, making the unauthorized state change observable. Inspired by EDB-40156; this is an original laboratory model of the specified boundary, not a reproduction of the affected product.
remediation: Remove the factory bypass from the remote request path and require an existing server-side administrator session. Session tokens are fixed synthetic credentials in this fixture, not a production session scheme. Tests inspect committed sessions and configuration rows; other weaknesses in the multi-issue EDB report are outside this case.

references.title: EDB-40156 — Ubee EVW3226 1.0.20 — factoryBypass authentication bypass (Gergely Eberhardt)

description: A query gateway checks restricted-table permissions only on its simple query branch. Adding an allowed WHERE or ORDER BY clause lets a reader retrieve private role rows from real SQLite queries. Inspired by EDB-44068; this is an original laboratory model of the specified boundary, not a reproduction of the affected product.
remediation: Authorize the resolved table before branching on query clauses. Table and sort identifiers are mapped from allowlists and filter values are bound as parameters in both variants, isolating the authorization weakness from SQL injection. Trusted fixture tokens determine roles; only the metadata-disclosure stage of the OrientDB report is modeled, not its later code-execution chain.

references.title: EDB-44068 — OrientDB — query-clause permission bypass / CVE-2017-11467 (SecuriTeam / Francis Alexander)

description: A local-path redirect check allows a slash followed by a backslash. Browsers interpreting backslashes as separators can treat the resulting Location as a network-path reference to an external host. Inspired by EDB-43592; this is an original laboratory model of the specified boundary, not a reproduction of the affected product.
remediation: After one strict percent-decoding pass, reject backslashes, control characters, residual percent encodings and any URL authority or scheme; allow only absolute local paths beginning with a single slash. Output is a Location model with no live browser. Tests normalize the browser separator behavior explicitly; this is not a complete WHATWG URL parser.

references.title: EDB-43592 — Oracle E-Business Suite — backslash open redirect / CVE-2017-3528 (Andrew Gill)

description: An original native C model of PHP2Shell request-cleanup corruption. A deterministic allocation failure interrupts replacement of request-owned memory; shutdown then reads freed storage. AddressSanitizer observes an actual use-after-free. This is not PHP itself, a multipart parser or an RCE reproduction.
remediation: Stage and initialize replacement allocations without publishing partial state. Handle allocation failure by returning to a safe cleanup point, preserving the old value until the replacement is complete. The failure is injected into tiny allocations, not caused by exhausting host memory. Real PHP requires the upstream runtime fix: its soft/hard OOM strategy is broader than this reduced transactional model.

references.title: PHP CVE-2026-109618 — RCE via OOM corruption
PHP security release — 21 October 2026

description: An original C worker-lifetime model of PHP2Shell stale request-owned globals. A fatal producer path or a late shutdown diagnostic leaves a global pointing into a freed request. A second request on the same modeled worker reads it before initialization; AddressSanitizer detects the actual use-after-free. No PHP runtime or exploit chain is embedded.
remediation: Clear worker references after all shutdown callbacks and before freeing their request-owned storage, including interrupted and late-diagnostic paths. Test both a pre-initialization warning and upload-progress-like consumer, plus controls with no consumer or a new worker. This models ownership and reset ordering only; actual PHP remediation is updating its runtime, not inserting userland session_start or relying on application filtering.

references.title: PHP CVE-2026-109619 — RCE via stale global state
PHP security release — 21 October 2026

description: An original C streaming-decoder model of Node2Shell/Brotli. An impossible block switch is confused with temporary input starvation. Repeated feeds append into a real eight-byte heap buffer until AddressSanitizer detects an out-of-bounds write. The simplified category/type/payload grammar is not a Brotli stream, and the fixture does not reproduce Node.js RCE.
remediation: Return a permanent format-error status for an impossible block switch, propagate it through literal, command and distance paths, and retain a staging-buffer capacity check. Short malformed streams must be rejected too, so a bounds check alone is an incomplete repair. The Node.js project rates this issue high; the CVE also has a critical CVSS v4 score. Real remediation is a fixed Node.js/Brotli runtime. See the named-CVE guide for sourced version boundaries.

references.title: Node.js CVE-2026-111497 — October 2026 security release
Brotli upstream block-switch correction, commit 0ed4268
Brotli 1.2.1 security release

description: An original C model of the Windows PHP-CGI best-fit argument boundary. A percent-encoded soft-hyphen byte becomes a dash after the CGI option guard, activating an internal synthetic include_private option. A real getopt parser consumes the resulting argv. No PHP runtime, Windows codepage API, script or system command is executed.
remediation: Normalize with the same byte mapping used by the option consumer before checking a dash-prefixed query. Preserve normal key/value query handling, reject malformed encodings and unsupported bytes, and limit the synthetic option to a fixed private-data marker. This models the best-fit bypass only; actual CVE remediation requires a corrected PHP-CGI runtime for the relevant Windows deployment.

EDB-52331 — PHP CGI Module argument injection

description: An original logging handler model inspired by Log4Shell. Nested expressions in untrusted message text invoke an offline naming-service callback and can include a synthetic private configuration value in that lookup. An actual log file records the final message. This is not Log4j/JNDI, LDAP networking, class loading or RCE.
remediation: Write untrusted log messages as data without expression evaluation. The vulnerable miniature interpreter accepts only bounded env and jndi-like lookups, resolves nested innermost expressions, and sends requests to a synthetic callback; it never uses eval or a real network. The application-level correction illustrates the boundary, while actual Log4Shell remediation is updating the affected log4j-core dependency and accounting for its subsequent advisories.

description: An original TeamCity-inspired dispatch model authenticates the initial public path but later forwards a JSP parameter to a protected administrative handler. A successful unauthorized request commits a synthetic administrator to SQLite. This is a route-identity model, not a TeamCity server or reproduction of its Java servlet implementation.
remediation: Resolve the effective target before authorization and enforce the administrator session on the final route, including forwards. Query parameters cannot supply a role; only the trusted session map determines access. The reduced JSP/semicolon grammar is explicit and bounded. Real TeamCity remediation is installing its patched product release.

description: An original Confluence-inspired pre-authentication expression-dispatch model evaluates path expressions while preparing a redirect. A restricted AST interpreter can set a response header to synthetic private state. The model demonstrates an evaluated-request boundary; it is not an OGNL engine, Java runtime, shell or complete Confluence RCE reproduction.
remediation: Treat the request path as data and percent-encode it when constructing the login redirect, without invoking an expression interpreter. The miniature vulnerable grammar exposes only setHeader with string or synthetic-secret arguments; it cannot load classes or execute system commands. Authentication later in dispatch does not protect earlier expression evaluation. Actual remediation requires a patched Confluence product.

description: Original reduced Python model inspired by CVE-2022-22965. A dotted-property binder traverses a synthetic class/module/class-loader graph and changes an internal access-log prefix. The sink writes a real local log to the altered filename. It models the binding boundary, not Spring, Tomcat, JSP writing or RCE.
remediation: Preflight an exact allowlist of client-editable properties, including an explicitly allowed nested profile field, before traversing or modifying the model. Log prefixes remain confined to a synthetic logs directory in both variants. Actual Spring remediation requires the vendor fix and consideration of the deployment prerequisites described in its advisory.

description: Original reduced Python model inspired by CVE-2024-23897. A CLI parser expands @file arguments before the command permission check. Its help error exposes the first line of a real synthetic private file. The reduced parser demonstrates pre-authorization disclosure only; it is not args4j, a Jenkins controller or the later RCE chain.
remediation: Disable @file expansion for remotely supplied CLI arguments. Keep those arguments literal rather than attempting to authorize after expansion. File expansion in the vulnerable model is bounded to existing files inside the fixture workspace and a small size; it never reads outside the laboratory working directory. Actual Jenkins remediation is upgrading or disabling the affected CLI.

references.title: Jenkins SECURITY-3314 / CVE-2024-23897 — official advisory

description: Original reduced Python model inspired by CVE-2022-40684. An appliance handler trusts a loopback identity claimed in client Forwarded and User-Agent headers. A forged request writes a synthetic administrator key marker to a real local file. No Fortinet code, SSH key or SSH login is involved.
remediation: Require an issued administrator token independent of client forwarding headers. Normalize header names and reject case-colliding duplicates before authorization. Real deployments must also authenticate trusted proxy or internal-service channels; this fixture models only the external request boundary.

references.title: Fortinet CVE-2022-40684 — vendor advisory
EDB-51092 — Fortinet forwarded-header authentication bypass

description: Original reduced Python model inspired by CVE-2023-22515. An internal setup-complete property is writable through a public binding path. A second request then enters the setup administrator handler and commits an unauthorized account to SQLite. This reduced stateful model is separate from the earlier Confluence expression-injection case.
remediation: Reject externally supplied internal setup properties and keep setup state in trusted storage. The setup route still supports legitimate initial installation using a server-controlled fresh-install fixture setting. The test environment flag is not client request data. Actual remediation is the patched Confluence release; this is not its Java or HTTP implementation.

references.title: Atlassian CVE-2023-22515 — broken access control advisory
EDB-51829 — Confluence setup authentication bypass

description: Original reduced Python model inspired by CVE-2023-7028. A reset request identifies a real account from one verified address but delivers the same recovery token to every supplied address, including an unverified recipient. Tests inspect a real synthetic outbox file. SMTP, password changes and GitLab application code are outside this model.
remediation: Resolve exactly one account and filter delivery recipients against its server-side verified addresses. Preserve valid secondary addresses and reject requests spanning multiple accounts. The token is a fixed laboratory marker so tests isolate recipient authorization, not token generation security. Real remediation requires the GitLab security update.

description: Original reduced Python model inspired by CVE-2023-28432. A distributed bootstrap verification handler returns synthetic server configuration without checking its peer token. Its response includes a root credential marker. The configuration is a trusted fixture dependency, not host environment collection; no real MinIO deployment or network service is used.
remediation: Authenticate the internode token before loading or serializing server configuration. A valid peer must retain access, while arbitrary self-asserted peer headers convey no privilege. Tests replace the configuration dependency with distinct values to verify the disclosure boundary. Actual remediation requires the MinIO fix.

description: Original reduced Python model inspired by CVE-2023-46604. A serialized throwable names a class selected from an offline registry. The vulnerable decoder constructs it before checking its exception type; a synthetic context-loader constructor parses XML and writes a real marker file. This models constructor side effects, not Java class loading, OpenWire bytes or broker RCE.
remediation: Validate the selected class against the permitted exception type before invoking any constructor. The registry is fixed laboratory code with no dynamic imports, and the XML context comes from an offline map. An error response after construction is too late to undo side effects. Actual ActiveMQ/OpenWire remediation requires the upstream fix in clients and brokers.

description: Original reduced Python model inspired by CVE-2024-42327. An authenticated user.get-like API concatenates requested role projection expressions into a real SQLite query. A scalar subquery retrieves another role's synthetic administrator token despite a bound outer role identifier. The model isolates SQL projection injection, not Zabbix or a full privilege-escalation chain.
remediation: Map requested projection identifiers through an exact allowlist and keep role identifiers bound. Reject the entire projection when any field is unknown; binding values does not make SQL identifiers safe. Preserve authorized multi-column requests and valid reader tokens. Actual remediation is the Zabbix security update.

description: Original reduced Python model inspired by CVE-2016-3714. A parsed SVG resource URL is substituted into a shell-based delegate command. A crafted resource writes a real local marker via the shell. The delegate is the local printf utility, never an image converter or downloader, so this exercises the shell boundary without contacting the URL or reproducing ImageMagick.
remediation: Pass the parsed resource as one positional argv element to a fixed executable, without a shell. Validate the bounded XML and expected resource scheme before delegation in both variants. The tests use only local printf commands and synthetic files. Real ImageMagick remediation also requires its security fixes and a suitable coder/delegate policy.

description: Original reduced Python model inspired by CVE-2023-25690. A rewrite handler decodes a client target and reinserts it into a serialized backend request. CRLF data turns one frontend input into two requests parsed by a real bounded backend parser. Tests observe serialized bytes on disk. This models request splitting, not Apache configuration, live sockets, chunked bodies or a full proxy deployment.
remediation: Reject controls and spaces after URL decoding and before interpolating the rewritten target. Keep validation and serialization on the same representation. The backend parser is a deliberately small GET/header grammar and does not claim HTTP compliance or coverage of all request-smuggling variants. Actual remediation requires the Apache HTTP Server fix and review of affected rewrite rules.
